title: Theo's Free Mug Cost Him $1,685 ☕
description:
Nora and Theo each keep $10,000 in savings. Theo's bank gave him a free mug. Nora's high-yield savings account gave her $350 a year instead of $38.

At the US national average savings rate of 0.38%, $10,000 earns about $38 in a year. At an assumed 3.5% APY it earns $350. That's a $312 gap in year one, and roughly $1,685 after five years ($1,877 vs $191) if the rates stayed the same.

The mug wasn't free. It was the most expensive mug in the cupboard.

What APY does your savings account pay right now? Drop the number below 👇

Follow for more numbers that change how you spend.

⚠️ Illustration only: $10,000 each, rates treated as APY and held constant for 5 years, interest left in the account, before tax. 0.38% = FDIC national average savings rate (Source: FDIC National Rates and Rate Caps, published 19 Oct 2026). 3.5% is an assumed high-yield rate; leading online savings accounts paid roughly 3-4% in autumn 2026, and rates change often. Check that any bank is FDIC insured. This is not financial advice.
